drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr1-02: weak_card: a truism (several producers on one topic). r1 keeps 9 cards without it; rewrites of sr1-04 and sr1-11 keep the true side at 4.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr1-08: duplicate of sr1-09 (partition-expansion-key-remapping). Its 'fixed partition count' qualifier gives away sr1-09's answer.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr1-12: weak_card: 'by default' implies a mode in which brokers deserialize values, and no such mode exists; it was also the only 'by default' in r1, on a false card. r1 stays at 9 cards (4T/5F).
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr2-02: weak_card: sr2-03 and sr2-07 give it away, because both treat retention as working per segment. r2 stays at 9 (5T/4F).
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr2-08: weak_card: the answer can be read from the value 'delete,compact', and the explanation copies the source sentence.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr2-10: weak_card: name giveaway. 'LogAppendTime' tells the player that the producer's timestamp is replaced, and the cited config entry does not say that the broker overwrites it.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr3-02: ambiguous: the 4.3 design page itself says that adding log.cleanup.policy=compact enables cleaning on a particular topic. The suggested replacement (a topic cleanup.policy overrides the broker default) only tests general override behaviour, which is the truism the r6 verifier flagged in sr6-06. No clean card is possible, so drop. r3 stays at 9 (4T/5F).
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr3-04: weak_card: it restates the delete.retention.ms description, and the answer can be read from the setting's name.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr3-09: weak_card: a truism, since the head of a compacted log keeps every record by definition. Dropping it also removes the hint its explanation gave to sr3-07.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr4-06: weak_card: true by definition ('expand a quorum by adding a controller'), and it tests an operator procedure outside r4's developer depth. r4 keeps 11 cards (5T/6F).
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr5-03: weak_card: a strawman ('equal leadership'), and sr5-04 and sr5-05 give it away by naming the single leader.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr5-11: weak_card: the distractor ('replica with the most recent write') makes little sense, and the card never reaches auto.leader.rebalance.enable. r5 keeps 10 cards (6T/4F).
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr6-01: duplicate of sr6-05 (acks=0 gives no broker feedback). Following the scan, I keep sr6-05 because it tests the concrete documented behaviour (offset -1), and sr6-01 is close to a definition of acks=0. Dropping it also removes a false card with a 'With acks=X' opener.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr6-06: weak_card: 'a topic-specific setting overrides the cluster default' is true of every per-topic override, and the card sits near ELR's cluster-level management of min.insync.replicas.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr6-09: weak_card: a truism, because every replicated system handles nodes that crash and recover. r6 stays at 9 (4T/5F) without the paired replacements.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr8-03: duplicate of sr8-02 (default automatic retries bounded by delivery.timeout.ms): knowing one answer gives the other. r8 keeps 11 cards (6T/5F).
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr9-10: weak_card: the answer can be read from the wording (seek() to an earlier offset rewinds). Dropping it also removes the hint it gave to sr1-03. r9 keeps 11 cards (5T/6F).
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr10-01: weak_card: a strawman, since nobody thinks a producer acknowledgement means downstream processing has finished; the cited page was also the introduction rather than the design section.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr10-04: weak_card: config-name trivia (which timeout bounds commitSync()). I did not use the suggested commitAsync replacement, because 'commitAsync() blocks' is a name giveaway.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr10-06: weak_card: a truism (overwriting by primary key makes duplicates harmless) with a true-marking 'can'. r10 stays at 9 (5T/4F).
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr11-06: duplicate of sr11-11, the other side of the client-versus-broker liveness-timer split. It is also near-trivial in the default classic context. r11 keeps 11 cards (5T/6F).
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr12-01: ambiguous, and no clean card is possible. The 4.3.1 KafkaProducer javadoc says 'If the transactional.id is set, idempotence is automatically enabled', but an explicit enable.idempotence=false with a transactional.id throws a ConfigException, which only the client source shows. Under default settings the card says no more than sr8-06, and the verifier's suggested replacement rests on behaviour the 4.3 docs do not state. r12 keeps 11 cards (5T/6F).
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr13-01: weak_card: the answer can be read from the wording, because 'the application that embeds the library' already says where the topology runs.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr13-07: weak_card: a name match (the Streams protocol with group.protocol=streams), and 'Since Kafka 4.2' is arguable because 4.1 early access already used that value. r13 keeps 10 cards (4T/6F).
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr14-01: weak_card: the explanation only repeats the statement, the statement can be guessed from its wording, and the cited page shows the fact only through a config example. r14 keeps 10 cards (5T/5F).
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr14-08: weak_card: a near strawman that confuses authentication (SASL) with authorization; it was also a fifth false card on the 'wrong actor' template.
drop.kafka-fundamentals-sr7-10: weak_card (it tested only the custom-Partitioner footnote, and 'its' was vague). I rewrote it with the verifier's replacement instead of dropping it: without it, r7's true statements would average 7.6 characters longer than the false ones, which breaks the deck's 5-character rule. With it the gap is 4.0. partitioner.ignore.keys entry: 'When set to true the producer won't use record keys to choose a partition ... this setting has no effect if a custom partitioner is used.' It joins sr7-12 as the second false card on the key-hash template, which is the cap. (final: drop: Name giveaway, raised by the wording lens (drop) and also by the fact lens. A config named ignore.keys that is set to true and 'still hashes a record's key' reads as false from the name alone. The fact is correct (producer configs: 'When set to true the producer won't use record keys to choose a partition'), but the card breaks the no-name-giveaway and no-strawman rules. Side effect: r7 length balance. Per the editor, without this card the true statements average 7.6 chars longer than the false ones. The orchestrator should fix that another way, for example by shortening sr7-09 (true, 117 chars).)

kafka-fundamentals-sr1-04.reason: weak_card (a truism with the wrong actor), rewritten rather than dropped because dropping it, sr1-02, sr1-08 and sr1-11 would leave r1 with 7 cards and 2 true. The new card covers the r1 item 'partitions spread over brokers'. Introduction: 'a topic is spread over a number of "buckets" located on different Kafka brokers'. (final: keep)
kafka-fundamentals-sr1-04.statement: Kafka spreads a topic's partitions over several brokers of the cluster.
kafka-fundamentals-sr1-04.explanation: A topic's partitions are buckets placed on different brokers, so client applications can read and write one topic through many brokers at the same time.

kafka-fundamentals-sr1-06.reason: explanation_error: the explanation never said that allow.auto.create.topics defaults to true, and the statement made the consumer's request depend on the broker setting. The broker is now the actor. Consumer configs: 'A topic being subscribed to will be automatically created only if the broker allows for it using auto.create.topics.enable ... Default: true'. (final: fixed)
kafka-fundamentals-sr1-06.statement: A broker with auto.create.topics.enable=true creates a missing topic when a KafkaConsumer subscribes.
kafka-fundamentals-sr1-06.explanation: allow.auto.create.topics defaults to true on the consumer, so the broker's auto.create.topics.enable decides whether a subscribed missing topic is created.

source.title: Kafka 4.3 Consumer and Share Consumer Configs

kafka-fundamentals-sr1-11.reason: weak_card (circular wording), rewritten to keep r1 at 9 cards with 4 true. The statement is shortened so that r1's true average (77.0) stays within 5 characters of the false average (73.0). Message format: 'Messages (aka Records) are always written in batches ... we could have a record batch containing a single record.' (final: keep)
kafka-fundamentals-sr1-11.statement: Kafka stores a record sent alone by a producer inside a record batch.
kafka-fundamentals-sr1-11.explanation: Kafka always writes records in record batches; a batch holds one or more records, so a lone record is stored as a single-record batch.

kafka-fundamentals-sr3-10.reason: ambiguous: the design page itself calls max.compaction.lag.ms a 'compaction deadline'. The new statement tests a hard guarantee, which the design page denies: 'Note that this compaction deadline is not a hard guarantee since it is still subjected to the availability of log cleaner threads and the actual compaction time.' (final: fixed)
kafka-fundamentals-sr3-10.statement: On a compacted topic, Kafka removes a superseded record before max.compaction.lag.ms has elapsed.
kafka-fundamentals-sr3-10.explanation: max.compaction.lag.ms bounds how long a record stays ineligible for compaction, but it is not a hard deadline: cleaning still depends on free log cleaner threads and compaction time.
kafka-fundamentals-sr3-10.misconception: max.compaction.lag.ms is a hard deadline by which superseded records are removed.

kafka-fundamentals-sr8-12.reason: explanation_error: 'subsequent producer API calls fail' holds only for transactional or producer-id fatal errors; a topic-level authorization failure fails only that record. The new source is the Callback javadoc, which lists 'Non-Retriable exceptions (fatal, the message will never be sent): ... AuthorizationException'. The statement and the answer are unchanged. (final: keep)
kafka-fundamentals-sr8-12.statement: KafkaProducer keeps retrying AuthorizationException until delivery.timeout.ms expires.
kafka-fundamentals-sr8-12.explanation: AuthorizationException is non-retriable: KafkaProducer does not resend that record and reports the failure to the send() callback instead.
kafka-fundamentals-sr8-12.misconception: Authorization failures are retried until the delivery deadline.

kafka-fundamentals-sr9-05.reason: source_problem: the Distribution page covers only offset storage. The KafkaConsumer javadoc states the fact: 'each process would have its own consumer group, so each process would subscribe to all the records published to the topic' and 'any number of consumer groups for a given topic without duplicating data'. The explanation now follows that source; the statement and the answer are unchanged. (final: fixed)
kafka-fundamentals-sr9-05.statement: Consumers with different group.id values share the same consumption position for a partition.
kafka-fundamentals-sr9-05.explanation: Each consumer group keeps its own offsets, so every group reads all records of a topic independently, and Kafka supports any number of groups on one topic without duplicating data.
kafka-fundamentals-sr9-05.misconception: Different groups share a common reading position.

kafka-fundamentals-sr9-12.reason: ambiguous: 'Since Kafka 4.2' rested the card on a release number, while per-record acknowledgement already existed in the 4.1 preview. I left out the verifier's 'rather than committing partition offsets' because the design page does not state it. Design page, share groups: 'Records are acknowledged individually ... Delivery attempts to consumers in a share group are counted ... partitions may be assigned to multiple consumers.' Keep appliesTo 'Kafka 4.2 and later' and volatility may_change. (final: fixed)
kafka-fundamentals-sr9-12.statement: In a share group, Kafka tracks the acknowledgement of each delivered record separately.
kafka-fundamentals-sr9-12.explanation: Share consumers acquire records under a time-limited lock and can acknowledge, release or reject each one; delivery attempts are counted, and a partition may feed several consumers.

kafka-fundamentals-sr11-05.reason: source_problem: the CooperativeStickyAssignor page only points to RebalanceProtocol, and that page states the fact: 'COOPERATIVE rebalance protocol allows a consumer to retain its currently owned partitions before participating in a rebalance event.' The explanation now links the assignor to the COOPERATIVE protocol; the statement and the answer are unchanged. (final: fixed)
kafka-fundamentals-sr11-05.statement: With CooperativeStickyAssignor, consumers keep ownership of their unmoved partitions throughout a rebalance.
kafka-fundamentals-sr11-05.explanation: With CooperativeStickyAssignor on every group member, rebalances are cooperative: a consumer retains its owned partitions, and only partitions that must move are revoked, then reassigned in a follow-up rebalance.

kafka-fundamentals-sr6-04.reason: tell: scan tell (1). The '<client> uses <wrong value> when <setting> is left unset' template was false in 5 of 6 cards. This changes only the wording; the fact (default acks=all) and the answer (false) are the same. (final: fixed)
kafka-fundamentals-sr6-04.statement: A KafkaProducer with default settings uses acks=1, where the leader responds without waiting for followers.
kafka-fundamentals-sr6-04.explanation: KafkaProducer defaults to acks=all: the leader waits for the full set of in-sync replicas to acknowledge a record before the request counts as complete.
kafka-fundamentals-sr6-04.misconception: The default acknowledgement mode is acks=1.

kafka-fundamentals-sr13-06.reason: tell: scan tell (1), the 'left unset' false template. Same fact (the default processing.guarantee is at_least_once) and same answer (false). (final: fixed)
kafka-fundamentals-sr13-06.statement: Kafka Streams runs with processing.guarantee=exactly_once_v2 unless an application overrides it.
kafka-fundamentals-sr13-06.explanation: Kafka Streams defaults processing.guarantee to at_least_once; an application gets exactly-once processing only by setting exactly_once_v2 explicitly.
kafka-fundamentals-sr13-06.misconception: Kafka Streams enables exactly_once_v2 processing by default.

kafka-fundamentals-sr14-05.reason: tell: scan tell (1), the 'left unset' false template. After this and the two rewrites above, 'left unset' carries only sr11-09 and sr14-03, which is the 2-card cap. Same fact (the default sasl.mechanism is GSSAPI) and same answer (false). (final: fixed)
kafka-fundamentals-sr14-05.statement: For SASL_SSL connections, KafkaProducer's default sasl.mechanism is PLAIN.
kafka-fundamentals-sr14-05.explanation: sasl.mechanism defaults to GSSAPI (Kerberos) for SASL connections, so a client that uses PLAIN has to set sasl.mechanism=PLAIN explicitly.
kafka-fundamentals-sr14-05.misconception: SASL_SSL selects PLAIN as the client's default authentication mechanism.

kafka-fundamentals-sr12-12.reason: tell: scan tell (5). 'automatically' marked false cards, and with sr12-01 dropped no true card used it. This removes 'can automatically' from a false card. Same fact (the application resets the consumer position after an abort) and same answer (false). (final: fixed)
kafka-fundamentals-sr12-12.statement: KafkaProducer.abortTransaction() also rewinds KafkaConsumer to the aborted transaction's input records.
kafka-fundamentals-sr12-12.explanation: After an abort, the application must reset the consumer position explicitly so that it reprocesses the records handled by the aborted transaction.
kafka-fundamentals-sr12-12.misconception: Aborting a producer transaction also restores the consumer's current position.

kafka-fundamentals-sr10-08.reason: tell: this removes a true-marking hedge ('can') and shortens a true r10 statement. The r10 drops had pushed the true average 5.4 characters above the false average; the gap is now about 3.8. Same fact and answer. KafkaConsumer javadoc: 'applications reading from topics with transactional messages will see gaps in the consumed offsets ... filtered out for consumers in both isolation levels'. (final: fixed)
kafka-fundamentals-sr10-08.statement: KafkaConsumer sees offset gaps on a transactional topic under either isolation level.
kafka-fundamentals-sr10-08.explanation: Transaction markers occupy offsets in the log, and KafkaConsumer filters them out of the records it returns, so the offsets of returned records skip them.
